newsitem.title: USA: P&G stock rises after results beat forecast.
newsitem.headline: P&G stock rises after results beat forecast.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co stock rose 5 to 112-5/8 after its second-quarter earnings beat Wall Street estimates, analysts said.
McDonald & Co analyst Saul Ludwig said the stock was up on "a great quarter... I think the stock is reflecting the very positive outlook that we see" for the company.
For the quarter ended December 31, P&G's earnings rose to $1.35 a primary share from $1.18 in the year-ago quarter. That compared with First Call's mean earnings estimate of $1.32.
"The corporate strategies are working," Morgan Stanley & Co analyst Brenda Landry said.

She said while a decline in commodity prices was part of the reason earnings increased, margins were helped by P&G's "everyday low" pricing policy and Efficient Consumer Response, an inventory and store-shelf management program under which P&G has eliminated cents-off packs, refund offers and other traditional promotions.
Landry said Wall Street may be starting to understand that while the program might initially dent sales volume, it builds margins and cash flow, and over time it boosts revenue.
She said P&G is adding capacity to produce paper products and she expects new products such as new toothpaste varieties.
Landry rates P&G a "strong buy," Ludwig a "solid hold."
